nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ divide $Q_9 = 210$, and let $p \ge 2$, $n$ and $j$ be natural numbers. Write $N_1(m, n) = n \cdot (Q_9/m)$. Then $\lfloor N_1(m, n)/p^j \rfloor$ equals the floor of the real number $Q_9 (n/p^j)/m$.
nodes.title: Legendre terms of $N_1$ as real floors

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ divide $Q_9 = 210$, and let $p \ge 2$, $n$ and $j$ be natural numbers. Write $N_{10}(m, n) = 10n \cdot (Q_9/m)$. Then $\lfloor N_{10}(m, n)/p^j \rfloor$ equals the floor of the real number $10 Q_9 (n/p^j)/m$.
nodes.title: Legendre terms of $N_{10}$ as real floors

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ divide $Q_9 = 210$, and let $p \ge 2$, $n$ and $j$ be natural numbers. Write $N_9(m, n) = 9n \cdot (Q_9/m)$. Then $\lfloor N_9(m, n)/p^j \rfloor$ equals the floor of the real number $9 Q_9 (n/p^j)/m$.
nodes.title: Legendre terms of $N_9$ as real floors

nodes.summary: The grid $G$-function for $k = 9$ satisfies $G_9(9) = 1$.
nodes.title: Value of $G_9$ at $9$

nodes.summary: For every natural number $j$, the grid $G$-function for $k = 9$ satisfies $G_9(j) = G_9(j \bmod 18900)$.
nodes.title: $G_9$ depends only on the residue modulo $18900$

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $o$ and $r$, the grid $G$-function for $k = 9$ satisfies $G_9(18900\,o + r) = G_9(r)$.
nodes.title: Periodicity of $G_9$ in multiples of $18900$

nodes.summary: For every natural number $j < 10$, the grid $G$-function for $k = 9$ satisfies $G_9(j) \le 1$.
nodes.title: Bound $G_9 \le 1$ below $10$

nodes.summary: For every natural number $j < 9$, the Breusch grid function $G_9$ satisfies $G_9(j) = 0$.
nodes.title: The Breusch grid function vanishes below 9

nodes.summary: For every real $x \ge 0$, the continuous Breusch function $G$ and the Breusch grid function $G_9$ satisfy $G(x) = G_9(\lfloor 18900x \rfloor)$.
nodes.title: The continuous Breusch function agrees with the grid function

nodes.summary: For every real $x \ge 0$, the continuous Breusch function $G$ satisfies $G(x) \le 3$.
nodes.title: The continuous Breusch function is at most 3

nodes.summary: Let $Q_9 = 210$. For every real $x \ge 1/(9 Q_9) = 1/1890$, if the continuous Breusch function $G$ satisfies $G(x) \ge 1$, then $x \ge 279/18900$.
nodes.title: Level-$1$ threshold for the continuous Breusch function

nodes.summary: Let $Q_9 = 210$. For every real $x \ge 1/(9 Q_9) = 1/1890$, if the continuous Breusch function $G$ satisfies $G(x) \ge 2$, then $x \ge 657/18900$.
nodes.title: Level-$2$ threshold for the continuous Breusch function

nodes.summary: Let $Q_9 = 210$. For every real $x \ge 1/(9 Q_9) = 1/1890$, if the continuous Breusch function $G$ satisfies $G(x) \ge 3$, then $x \ge 963/18900$.
nodes.title: Level-$3$ threshold for the continuous Breusch function

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $n \ge 1$ and $j$ be natural numbers. If $p^j > 2100n$, then the continuous Breusch function $G$ satisfies $G(n/p^j) = 0$.
nodes.title: The continuous Breusch function vanishes at small ratios

nodes.summary: For every real $x$ with $0 \le x < 1/2100$, the continuous Breusch function $G$ satisfies $G(x) = 0$.
nodes.title: The continuous Breusch function vanishes near zero

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $t$ and $d$, the floor of the real number $t/d$, as an integer, equals the natural-number quotient of $t$ by $d$ (rounded down), as an integer. Both sides are $0$ when $d = 0$, since division by zero is $0$ for both real numbers and natural numbers.
nodes.title: Integer cast of the floor of a quotient of natural numbers

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $N$ and $b$ be natural numbers with $\lfloor \log_p N \rfloor < b$, where $\lfloor \log_p N \rfloor$ is taken to be $0$ when $N = 0$. Then the exponent of $p$ in $N!$, as an integer, equals $\sum_{j=1}^{b-1} \lfloor N / p^j \rfloor$.
nodes.title: Legendre's formula with integer summands

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $p$ and $n$, $\nu_p(n)$ is the integer $\sum_{d \mid 210} \mu(d)\bigl(v_p((2100n/d)!) - v_p((1890n/d)!) - v_p((210n/d)!)\bigr)$, where $\mu$ is the Möbius function and $v_p(m)$ is the exponent of $p$ in the prime factorization of $m$ (zero when $p$ is not prime).
nodes.title: The $p$-adic valuation of the weighted product

nodes.summary: For a pair $(m, \varepsilon)$ of a natural number $m$ and an integer $\varepsilon$, and natural numbers $p$ and $n$, let $a = \lfloor 210/m \rfloor$ (so $a = 0$ when $m = 0$). The term is the integer $\varepsilon\bigl(v_p((10na)!) - v_p((9na)!) - v_p((na)!)\bigr)$, where $v_p(k)$ is the exponent of $p$ in the prime factorization of $k$ (zero when $p$ is not prime).
nodes.title: One divisor's contribution to the valuation

nodes.summary: Let $Q = 210$, let $m \ge 1$ be a divisor of $Q$, and let $n$, $p$ be natural numbers. Write $N = n \cdot (Q/m)$ and $R_m(n) = (10N)! / ((9N)! \, N!)$. Then, as integers, $v_p(R_m(n)) = v_p((10N)!) - v_p((9N)!) - v_p(N!)$, where $v_p(k)$ is the exponent of $p$ in the prime factorization of $k$ (zero when $p$ is not prime).
nodes.title: Valuation of a factorial ratio as a difference of valuations
